messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Incident 1775212345 - High CPU + pod evictions in serving-prod-us-west. Alerts: > 90% CPU on tokenizer-worker pools, multiple OOMKilled events. Paging sre-oncall.
sre-oncall: on it. seeing alerts for tokenizer-worker-* pods evicted across 3 nodes. linking logs now.
alex r: I can take triage. Any customer-facing errors showing?
maria g: yes, some 5xx spikes for /v1/generate for a handful of customers (hosted). latency up ~3-4x.
sre-oncall: Quick snapshot from k8s: ```kubectl get pods -n serving -l app=tokenizer-worker -o wide
NAME                           READY  STATUS     RESTARTS  AGE
tokenizer-worker-7f8b9c4d5-x2  0/1    Evicted    0         1h
tokenizer-worker-7f8b9c4d5-x3  0/1    OOMKilled  1         45m
tokenizer-worker-6a4d2e1f1-y1  1/1    Running    0         3h
```
logs show `oom-kill` and `SIGKILL` during heavy prompt batches.
sahil: attaching snippet from pod log: ```2026-03-15T18:02:12Z tokenizer INFO prompt_parse: received 12k tokens in batch, buffer_size=524288
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z tokenizer ERROR memory: allocation failure, attempting free...
2026-03-15T18:02:12Z kernel: Out of memory: Kill process 23456 (tokenizer) score 1234 or sacrifice child```
jess: looks like a sudden prompt/parse fanout from a customer job. Could be a malformed client sending long prompt arrays. Any matching request traces?
eng-ml: pulling traces now. There's a pattern from a single API key - `acct_89xx` - high throughput, lots of very long system prompts plus few-shot arrays. We should throttle that key immediately.
alex r: Agreed. Maria, can you block/throttle that API key on the rate-limiter?
maria g: Doing it now. `rate-limit update acct_89xx --qps=1 --burst=5` -> applied.
kevin: Also flipping a temporary autoscale policy to add more tokenizer workers to handle in-flight queues: `kubectl scale deploy tokenizer-worker --replicas=10 -n serving`
ops-bot: Autoscale triggered: added 5 replicas, pending scheduling. Noted: cluster has limited CPU headroom on three nodes.
sre-oncall: Because nodes are near capacity, scheduler is evicting pods (taint pressure). For immediate mitigation I recommend: 1) throttle offending key (done), 2) cordon one problematic node and drain low-priority batch pods to free CPU for tokenizer, 3) restart tokenizer pods with a lower initial token buffer env var.
eng-runtime: We can set `MAX_BUFFER_TOKENS=4096` env override to reduce memory ramps. Rolling restart in progress: `kubectl rollout restart deploy/tokenizer-worker -n serving`
sahil: note: changing MAX_BUFFER_TOKENS will change latency for some long prompts, but prevents OOM. We should pair with a canary before full rollout.
alex r: Can we patch deployment with canary subset first? `kubectl patch deploy/tokenizer-worker -p '{"spec":{"replicas":2}}'` and label canary=true
eng-runtime: Canary started on two pods with MAX_BUFFER_TOKENS=4096. Monitoring memory.
incident-bot: Customer impact: ~4.8% of requests returned 5xx in last 30m; top affected region us-west. No data exfiltration.
maria g: Enterprise customer AcmeCorp reported errors to CSM. Notifying account team.
jess: rolling drain on node ip-10-0-12-7 to free CPU for critical pods now. `kubectl drain ip-10-0-12-7 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` in progress.
ops-bot: Drain complete. Scheduler rescheduled pending tokenizer pods onto ip-10-0-15-9 (new node with spare capacity).
eng-ml: Canary pods stable, memory usage ~60% vs previous 120% peaks. No OOMs in canary.
sre-oncall: Good. Proceeding to roll the rest with the buffer change. Watch for regressions.
kevin: After buffer change and throttle, 5xx rate dropped to 0.9% over last 10m. Latency back to ~1.2x baseline.
alex r: Handing off to night oncall: @sre-night on duty. Summary in #oncall-handoffs. Followups: ticket infra-5823 to add request-size-enforcement on edge, ticket runtime-491 to implement adaptive buffering, and customer outreach to AcmeCorp (assigned to maria g).
sre-oncall: Handoff note: root cause appears to be abusive request pattern causing tokenizer to allocate large per-request buffers. Mitigations applied: throttled API key, lowered MAX_BUFFER_TOKENS via canary -> rollout, cordoned/drained node to free CPU. Observability: added a new alert for per-key token rate exceeding 200k tokens/min.
eng-runtime: Postmortem owner: alex r. Timeline and logs saved to /incidents/1775212345/artifacts.
maria g: Pinged AcmeCorp CSM, offered incident summary and temporary mitigations.
kevin: Leaving a runbook note: if tokenizer memory spikes, prefer throttling offending keys + reducing buffer over immediate cluster scale to avoid cascading evictions.
sre-oncall: Closing slack thread for now. Will reopen if errors >1% persist. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
